title: Protocol for in vivo and in vitro study of lymphatic valve formation driven by shear stress signaling pathway
protocol: Add 0.5 mL of 100% EtOH to a 50 mL tube.
Measure 200 mg tamoxifen powder using a METTLER TOLEDO scale and dissolve it in the 0.5 mL EtOH.
Mix 9.5 mL safflower oil into the tube containing dissolved tamoxifen.
Tape the tube to a test tube rocker for ∼16 h mixing.
Seal the cap with Parafilm and cover the entire 50 mL tube with aluminum foil.
Check daily to ensure all powder is dissolved before aliquoting desired amount of tamoxifen.
Inject tamoxifen intraperitoneally for pregnant dams and subcutaneously for postnatal pups on required dates.
Euthanize pregnant dams by CO2 asphyxiation followed by cervical dislocation.
Wet the abdomen of the euthanized dam with 70% EtOH.
Make a superficial incision in the skin using dissecting scissors without cutting through the peritoneal sac.
Cut across the skin longitudinally to reveal the peritoneal sac.
Create an incision in the peritoneal membrane and cut across longitudinally to expose the uterine horn.
Excise the uterine horn from the body.
Place the excised uterine horn in ice cold 1× PBS.
Cut through the uterine membrane to uncover individual embryos.
Peel the amniotic sac enveloping each embryo and separate them from the placenta.
Transfer the embryos to a 10 cm dish with ice cold 1× PBS.
Clip off about 2 mm of the tail for genotyping.
Place the tails in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Replace the PBS solution if it becomes bloody.
Keep embryos away from each other in the dish.
Clean scissors used for tailing with 70% EtOH between embryos.
Euthanize the embryos by decapitation.
Pin the embryos onto a sylgard 184 pad.
Create an incision on the ventral lower abdominal skin using spring scissors.
Cut across the abdomen longitudinally to expose the peritoneal sac.
Separate the layer of skin from the peritoneal sac gently.
Cut connections whenever necessary from mid abdomen to back left of the fetus.
Repeat the process on the right side of the fetus.
Create an incision in the peritoneal membrane on the ventral lower abdomen using spring scissors.
Cut across longitudinally towards the neck, exposing the organs of the peritoneal cavity.
Push the intestines and stomach to the left using the blunt end of the iris forceps.
Snip the connections between the mesentery and other organs as necessary.
Isolate the mesentery from the duodenum to the ileum by excising the cecum and the stomach.
Pin out the mesentery on a sylgard 184 pad starting from the duodenum in a clockwise manner into a ring.
Create multiple rings of the mesentery if necessary.
Use 1% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for tissue fixation.
Fix tissues in 1% PFA in PBS (1×) + NaN3 (0.05%) for approximately 16 hours at 4°C.
Wash the fixed tissues three times, each wash lasting 10 minutes with PBS (1×) + NaN3 (0.05%) on an orbital shaker at 4°C.
Euthanize pups injected with TM using an intraperitoneal ketamine overdose followed by cervical dislocation.
Create a ventral incision on the lower abdominal skin of a pup to reveal the peritoneal sac.
Cut longitudinally across the peritoneal membrane to expose its contents.
Use iris forceps to move intestines and stomach to the left, cutting connections between organs as needed.
Collect mesentery from duodenum to ileum by excising the stomach and cecum.
Pin the collected mesentery as a ring on a sylgard 184 pad under a dissecting microscope.
Mix 2% PFA with PBS (1×) + NaN3 (0.05%) to create the fixative solution.
Fix mesenteries with the prepared fixative solution for approximately 16 hours on an orbital shaker at 4°C.
Wash fixed tissue three times, each time for 10 minutes in PBS (1×) + NaN3 (0.05%) on an orbital shaker at 4°C to remove excess fixative.
Slice the bottom corners of P21 pup ears using a feather scalpel to create a gap between inner and outer sides.
Remove the inner side skin with cartilage layer from the outer side skin of the ear using precision tweezers, ensuring no cartilage is left on the vascular dermis.
Pin down the outer side skin of the excised ear on a sylgard 184 pad, placing it vascular side up for further processing.
Fix ear tissue in 2% PFA in PBS (1×) + NaN3 (0.05%) for approximately 16 hours on an orbital shaker at 7°C.
Wash the tissue three times for 10 minutes each with PBS + NaN3 (0.05%) on an orbital shaker at 4°C.
Cut through the sternum to split the ribcage and reveal organs of the pleural cavity.
Hold the costal muscles with iris forceps and snip at the muscle to release the diaphragm from the lower ribcage.
Snip all around the costal muscles to separate the diaphragm from the ribcage and liver.
Separate the diaphragm from the vertebral column.
Pin the diaphragm on a sylgard 184 pad with the central tendon domain side up.
Clean the central tendon domain of any connective tissue.
Fix the diaphragm in 2% PFA + PBS (1×) + NaN3 (0.05%) for approximately 16 hours on an orbital shaker at 4°C.
Wash the tissue three times for 10 minutes each with PBS + NaN3 (0.05%) on an orbital shaker at 4°C.
Fix the tissues in PFA at 4°C immediately after pinning them on sylgard pads.
Submerge an E16.5 tail in 100 μL of 50 mM NaOH.
Submerge an E18.5 or postnatal tail in 200 μL of 50 mM NaOH.
Place the tubes containing tails and NaOH solution in a heating block set to 95°C for 25 minutes.
Let the samples cool down after heating.
Neutralize E16.5 tail samples with 20 μL of 1 M Tris-HCl pH 7.5.
Neutralize E18.5 or postnatal tail samples with 40 μL of 1 M Tris-HCl pH 7.5.
Vortex the samples to mix reagents thoroughly.
Centrifuge the samples at 13,000 g (10,730 rpm) for 3 minutes.
Use the samples immediately or store them at -20°C.
Perform a standard PCR on a Biometra TRIO thermal cycler to genotype the tail samples.
Prepare an agarose gel according to standard protocol.
Run the PCR product through the agarose gel to separate genomic bands by size.
Image the gel using a BioRad ChemiDoc XRS+ system.
Permeabilize fixed tissues with 4 mL of PBS (1×) + NaN3 (0.05%) + 0.3% Triton (PBST) per dish for at least 1 hour.
Block samples in 3% donkey serum in 2 mL PBST per dish for at least 2 hours.
Prepare primary antibodies in 1.5 mL PBST per dish.
Incubate samples with the prepared primary antibodies and mix for approximately 16 hours at 4°C.
Wash samples with 4 mL PBST five times, each wash lasting 10 minutes.
Prepare secondary antibodies in 1.5 mL PBST in a dark-bodied tube.
Incubate samples in secondary antibodies for 1.5 hours on an orbital shaker at 20°C–22°C in a black-out box to prevent light exposure.
Wash samples with 4 mL PBST, 5 times, 10 minutes each.
Incubate samples in DAPI (1 μg/mL) for 5 minutes.
Wash samples with 4 mL PBS + NaN3 (0.05%), once for 5 minutes.
Mount the tissues on slides with mounting media.
Place a cover slip on top of the tissues without any bubbles.
Store tissues in mounting media at 4°C if mounting on another day.
Do not store samples in PBS + NaN3 (0.05%) before imaging.
Image immunostained slides using a Zeiss V16 fluorescence microscope.
Image tissues for lymphatic valve counting, measuring lymphatic vessel length, and diameter using a Leica SP8 confocal fluorescence microscope.
Image the whole ring of pinned out mesenteric lymphatic vessels under a Zeiss V16 fluorescence microscope with Zen Pro software.
Capture images of each mesenteric collecting lymphatic vessel and its branches under a Zeiss V16 microscope.
Overdose and euthanize the TM injected postnatal pup with ketamine followed by cervical dislocation.
Place the euthanized pup abdomen side up on a flat surface.
Wet the abdominal skin using 70% EtOH.
Create an incision on the skin.
Cut longitudinally towards the neck to reveal the peritoneal sac.
Create an incision on the peritoneal membrane and cut longitudinally towards the neck to expose the organs of the peritoneum and pleural cavity.
Make lateral cuts on the skin all the way to the back to expose the ribcage and the organs inferior to it.
Place the animal on its left side, so the right side is facing up, on a flat surface.
Place a sylgard 184 semicircular pad next to the belly of the animal to serve as a stage to pin the mesentery for easy imaging.
Use 1× PBS to hydrate the mesentery at all times during dissection and imaging.
Carefully expose the part of the mesentery inferior to the pancreas using iris forceps.
Place pins wherever necessary to expose the full length of the vessel.
Capture an image of the GFP positive mesentery under the V16 microscope using the Zen Pro software.
Acquire images in the GFP channel under low and high magnification of each collecting lymphatic vessel.
Expose the mesenteric lymphatic vessels of the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.
Capture images displaying the lymphatic vessel arising from the lymph node to the gut.
Capture higher magnification images of the lymphatic vessels and valves from representative branches.
Excise and pin the ear, inner vascular side up, on a sylgard 184 pad.
Image the ear tissue under a fluorescence microscope.
Obtain higher magnification images, for example 32×, for valve quantification.
Coat required number of wells of 6-well plates with fibronectin at 2 μg/cm² in 1 mL DPBS per well.
Incubate coated plates at 37°C, 5% CO₂ for 30 minutes.
Prepare complete endothelial cell growth medium MV2 by adding supplement mix to the endothelial cell basal medium MV2 according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Thaw frozen hdLECs cryovial in a 37°C water bath until very little frozen solution remains.
Quickly and generously spray the vial with 70% EtOH, wipe the tube.
Transfer the contents into the 15 mL tube containing Endothelial Cell Growth Medium MV 2.
Centrifuge the cellular suspension for 5 min at 400 g at 20°C–22°C.
Quickly remove the supernatant media and resuspend the pellet with 1 mL of Endothelial Cell Growth Medium MV 2.
Pipette up and down to create a homogenous cell resuspension.
Add the remaining Endothelial Cell Growth Medium MV 2 to make the full volume cell resuspension (1.5 mL media in each well).
Remove the fibronectin using a vacuum aspiration system inside of the hood.
Add 1.5 mL of cell resuspension to each well.
Rock the plate back and forth and side to side to ensure equal distribution of cells.
Incubate the cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 in a cell culture incubator.
Coat required wells of 6-well plates with 2 μg/cm² fibronectin per well and incubate for 30 min.
Seed 1 × 10⁵ cells per well of a 6-well plate.
Remove Endothelial Cell Growth Medium MV 2 from the cultured wells.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of DPBS.
Incubate the wells with 1 mL of 0.5% Trypsin-EDTA for 3 min at 37°C, 5% CO2 in a cell culture incubator.
Check if cells are floating in the well after 3 min.
If not, incubate for another minute and check again as necessary.
Once cells have detached from the plate, add 1 mL of Endothelial Cell Growth Medium MV 2 to stop trypsinization.
Collect the cell suspension in a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet with 1 mL of Endothelial Cell Growth Medium MV 2.
Pipette up and down to create a homogenous cell resuspension.
Mix 10 μL of cell resuspension with 10 μL of trypan blue dye.
Load 10 μL of cell-dye mixture onto commercial slides for counting cells using LUNA-II automated cell counter.
Add the required amount of Endothelial Cell Growth Medium MV 2 to make up the required volume.
Pipette 1.5 mL of cell resuspension into each fibronectin-coated well of 6-well plates.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 in a cell culture incubator.
Place a 70% EtOH-soaked 22 × 22 mm² coverslip standing up on each well of the 6-well plate using forceps.
Air-dry the coverslip for 30 minutes.
Coat the coverslip containing wells with fibronectin at 2 μg/cm².
Incubate the coated coverslips in a humidified cell culture incubator for 30 minutes.
Remove the fibronectin from the wells using vacuum aspiration.
Passage hdLECs onto the fibronectin-coated coverslip containing wells.
Change the media every 48 hours for hdLECs.
Seed 1 × 10^5 cells per well to start the culture.
Remove Endothelial Cell Growth Medium MV2 from 90%–95% confluent cells.
Perform polybrene-mediated lentiviral shscramble/shRNA infection at a MOI of 120 for 48 hours.
Incubate the plates in a cell culture incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Replace with fresh complete endothelial cell growth medium after designated treatment time.
Dispose of media containing lentiviruses in freshly made 10% bleach.
Add 1.5 mL Endothelial Cell Growth Medium MV 2 for static conditions.
Add 1 mL Endothelial Cell Growth Medium MV 2 for flow conditions.
Prepare the rocker in the incubator and set to 18 rpm at a 48° angle.
Place the plate on the rocker in a humidified cell culture incubator for required time.
Quantify valve gene expression using qRT-PCR, western blot, and/or immunostaining after exposure to flow conditions for 48 hours.
Quantify phosphorylated proteins using western blot and/or immunostaining after exposure to flow conditions for 10/30/60 minutes.
Follow manufacturer’s protocol to extract total RNA from hdLECs using Qiagen RNeasy® Plus Mini Kit.
Use RNase free tubes for RNA extraction.
Use 350 μL buffer RLT plus 3.5 μL β-mercaptoethanol (BME) to collect RNA from two wells of a 6-well plate with fully confluent cells.
Add 15–25 μL RNase free water to the spin column membrane, wait 1 min before centrifuging.
Pipette 2 μL RNase free water control onto two microspots of the Take3 microvolume plate and pipette 2 μL of samples onto the microspot.
Read the plate using an absorbance reader for RNA concentration without lid.
Store the RNA samples at -80°C for long-term storage.
Thaw RNA samples on ice.
Perform reverse transcription using 1,000 ng RNA sample.
Synthesize cDNA following Advantage RT-for-PCR kit instructions.
Dilute cDNA with Ultrapure distilled water at a ratio of 1:16 for qRT-PCR.
Store RNA and cDNA at -80°C for long-term use.
Thaw TaqMan probes on ice well in advance.
Prepare PCR master mix by pipetting TaqMan fast mix and Taqman probe into an Eppendorf tube.
Pipette 5.5 μL PCR master mix into each well of a 384 well plate.
Add 4.5 μL cDNA template to each well after adding the master mix.
Culture the cells on glass coverslips.
Remove the media and wash the cells with PBS once.
Fix the cells with 4% PFA for 12 min at 20°C–22°C.
Wash three times with PBS (1X)+NaN3 (0.05%), 5 min each time.
Permeabilize the cells with 0.1% triton+PBS (1X)+NaN3 (0.05%) for 20 min at 20°C–22°C.
Block the cells with 3% donkey serum in PBS (1X)+NaN3 (0.05%) (blocking buffer) for 30 min to 1 h at 20°C–22°C.
Dilute the antibodies in the blocking buffer according to the concentration.
Add primary antibodies and incubate in a wet box for ∼16 h at 4°C.
Wash three times with PBS (1X)+NaN3 (0.05%), 5 min each time.
Dilute the secondary antibodies in PBS (1X)+NaN3 (0.05%) according to the concentration.
Add secondary antibodies and incubate in a wet box for 1 h at 20°C–22°C.
Wash three times with PBS (1X)+NaN3 (0.05%), 5 min each time.
Mount with mounting media and image.
